title: Hold the Set, Pin the Judge
tagline: Correctness of the content and reliability of the shape are different axes. Measure both.

story.problem: A single-pass sweep over fifteen labelled vendor replies scored DeepSeek-V4-Flash 15/15 at less cost than the incumbent, so the classifier was switched to it. The very next run of the same fifteen cases scored 11/15 with six schema failures. One pass over a small set cannot separate two models near the top — it can only rule out the clearly worse — and an accuracy sweep is structurally blind to schema failure, because a call that never returns an object is not a wrong answer, it is no answer, and it averages in as a tie.
story.solution: Hold one human-labelled set constant across every candidate and run the production classifier over it rather than a copy. Count a fallback to the production keyword heuristic as a loss for the candidate, not a free pass. Run three rounds and rank on the worst round, with cost only as the third tiebreak. Measure shape conformance as its own axis with a probe that ignores the labels entirely and keeps every error string. Pin the judge to its own NEBIUS_JUDGE_MODEL so swapping the agent's model cannot move the bar, and ask it two independent questions rather than one blended score. Have both architectures emit one shared RunResult contract so a single stack-blind grader scores them with identical code.
story.outcome: The classifier was reverted to Qwen3-235B, which has now held 15/15 on the labelled set across three separate runs. The schema probe over thirty structured-output calls each read 30/30 against 26/30; a fresh single-round probe on 2026-08-30 read 15/15 against 3/15, with twelve AI_NoObjectGeneratedError failures. The same discipline vetoed a cheaper specialist model that produced 10/22 with all ten child sessions failed; reverting it and deleting a redundant outputSchema gave 33/37, then 52/53. No scorecard from npm run grade over the two committed RunResult files is published yet, and the planner role still has no eval that measures its prose.

prerequisites: Recipe 01 (Foundation) — the judge is a role in the model registry, not a constant
NEBIUS_API_KEY in .env.local — every script here makes real Token Factory calls, none mock a model
Node 24 (engines in package.json) and `npm install` at the repository root
KV_REST_API_URL and KV_REST_API_TOKEN, optional — without them the scripts print and skip the /observe summary
LANGSMITH_API_KEY, optional — eval:replies also files the run as a LangSmith experiment
A running deployment for eval:scout, which drives real planning turns and spends research credits

quickstart.clone: git clone https://github.com/jaredwerba/vendor-scout.git && cd vendor-scout && npm install
quickstart.configure: Create .env.local with NEBIUS_API_KEY (full list in README.md). KV and LangSmith keys are optional — without them results stay on stdout.
quickstart.run: PROBE_ROUNDS=1 npm run probe:schema -- Qwen/Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct-2507 deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash
